{{WorldTableTennisChampionshipsEvents|year=2013}}
[[File:Mondial Ping - Women's Singles - Final - Li Xiaoxia.jpg|thumbnail|right|Winner Li Xiaoxia playing at the event]]
{{main|2013 World Table Tennis Championships}}
[[Ding Ning]] was the defending champion but lost in the semifinals to [[Li Xiaoxia]]. Ding Ning had won the last two World Tennis Championships, 2011 and 2012.<ref>[http://www.ittf.com/ittf_tournaments/ittf_entries_wttc_web2.asp?Gender=W&Tour_ID=2190&Singles=1 Entry list]</ref> Li went on to win the title by defeating [[Liu Shiwen]] 11–8, 4–11, 11–7, 12–10, 6–11, 13–11 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ittf.com/_front_page/ittf_full_story1.asp?ID=31617&Competition_ID=2190&|title=The Olympic Champion is the World Champion, Li Xiaoxia Wins in Paris|date=2013-05-19|work=ittf.com}}</ref>

==Seeds==
Singles matches were best of 7 games in qualification matches and best of 7 games in the 128-player sized main draw.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ittf.com/world_events/wttc_2013/Playing_system_WTTC2013.pdf |title=2013 World TT Championships Playing System |publisher=ITTF |format=PDF |accessdate=11 May 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ittf.com/ittf_tournaments/ittf_entries_wttc_web2.asp?Gender=W&Tour_ID=2190&Singles=1&Seeded_Singles=1 |title=2013 WTTC Seeds&nbsp;– Women's singles |work=ittf.com |accessdate=11 May 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130608074843/http://www.ittf.com/ittf_tournaments/ittf_entries_wttc_web2.asp?Gender=W&Tour_ID=2190&Singles=1&Seeded_Singles=1 |archivedate=8 June 2013 }}</ref>
